ident.definition: A: in an optical-spectroscopic or radio/VLBI/blazar catalogue; B: photometric/mid-IR only

ruwe.definition: A: RUWE < 1.012038 (Quaia median), B: RUWE >= median

A_constraint.statement: Part A (offset curvature / EDR3 baseline) is a scale, not a bound: a static radio-optical offset produces no proper motion, a varying centroid can produce proper motion unrelated to the net offset, and the noise of the offset curvature is kept. Its Q exceeds the observed spin6 Q for every clip, so it cannot constrain frame leakage; only Part B constrains a G/BP-RP-dependent frame.

B_bound.scope: Cell frames drawn from N(complement fit, complement fit covariance); the noise-only row draws N(0, same covariance) and shows how much of the leak is fit noise.

B_insample_diagnostic.label: Quaia (G,BP-RP) cell frames ignoring z (in-sample degeneracy diagnostic)

SCAN_NULL.json__script_versions.note: Receipts in the pre_fix groups were written before gaia_estimator.provenance() hashed the __main__ script, so they carry no gaia_scan_null.py SHA-256 (their gaia_estimator.py SHA-256 is recorded per kind). The pre_fix_A / pre_fix_B split is the only receipt-visible difference between those earlier versions. replay_check reruns the first draws of every stored run (same kind, seed, calibration and amplitude) with the current script, whose SHA-256 is recorded in the replay receipt; BIT_IDENTICAL means every stored array agrees bit for bit on those draws, i.e. the stored run is reproduced by that identified script version for the compared draws (later draws of the same loop are not re-executed).
